look_here_first: This is a WOODY branching shrub with SMALL BLUE to lavender flowers (often ~10–13 mm long), rough/hairy ovate leaves with serrated/wavy edges. Do not describe its leaves as categorically smaller than autumn sage: sizes overlap (ballotiflora ~15–38 mm vs greggii ~8–48 mm in descriptions). More useful split: balloon-flower shrub sage's distinctly textured leaf faces and tiny blue-purple corollas versus S. greggii's generally smoother leaf blades with larger often ~25-mm showy corollas. Hays introduced-from-Medina specimen is NOT proof this is wild native in Hays.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small ovate leaves with serrate/wavy margins

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: At close range, inspect the hairy calyx/corolla tube and upper-lip hairs; Joey notes flowers around 10 mm across.

key_traits.label: Flower detail
key_traits.text: Showy for its size but MUCH smaller than S. greggii in comparison: blue to lavender-purple bilabiate flowers about 10–13 mm; hair on upper corolla lip/calyx, which requires focused macro.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey also notes pleasant volatile compounds/aromatic character in the leaves; treat odor as a supporting cue, not a primary ID character.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite ovate leaves roughly 15–38 mm, often coarsely toothed or crenulate/wavy, hair roughness on upper and lower faces; dimensions may overlap S. greggii.

key_traits.label: Comparison to greggii
key_traits.text: S. greggii also woody and may have similarly small leaves, but many cultivated S. greggii have large ~25 mm corollas and comparatively smooth elliptic foliage; don't rely on leaf LENGTH alone.

key_traits.label: Hays flora context
key_traits.text: UT Austin Hays flora specifically lists Salvia ballotiflora as introduced from a cliff above Medina River (Medina County) to Hays collection. This is not wild in-situ Hays nativity proof; keep historical introduction separate from source-pool learner inclusion.
